report.summary: (model supplied no summary; its answer is preserved in handoff)

handoff.purpose: Module docstring, constants, hashing, identity/paths, and secret floor scan helpers for the hash-chained council transcript.

symbols.name: ENTRY_VERSION
symbols.note: String 'dcouncil/1' identifying the record format.

symbols.name: ANCHOR_VERSION
symbols.note: String 'dcouncil-anchor/1' identifying the anchor format.

symbols.name: ROOT
symbols.note: Path to the repository root, resolved from this file's location.

symbols.name: DEFAULT_COUNCIL_DIR
symbols.note: Path to runs/council under ROOT.

symbols.name: _FORBIDDEN_STORE_DIR
symbols.note: Path to ROOT/memory, the directory council stores must never resolve under.

symbols.name: TURN_STATUS
symbols.note: Tuple of five allowed turn statuses: spoke, refused, unavailable, budget_exhausted, anomaly.

symbols.name: UNAVAILABLE_REASONS
symbols.note: Tuple of fixed machine reasons for unavailable status.

symbols.name: ANOMALY_REASONS
symbols.note: Tuple of fixed machine reasons for anomaly status.

symbols.name: PARTICIPANT_OUTCOMES
symbols.note: Tuple of participant outcome labels: requested, seated, responded, refused, unavailable.

symbols.name: MAX_CONTENT_CHARS
symbols.note: Integer 200000, fail-closed ceiling on a single turn's content size.

symbols.name: _ACTOR_RE
symbols.note: Compiled regex for council actor ids per ADR-010.

symbols.name: _COUNCIL_ID_RE
symbols.note: Compiled regex for council id filename safety.

symbols.name: _SHA256_RE
symbols.note: Compiled regex matching a 64-hex SHA256 digest.

symbols.name: _WRITE_LOCK
symbols.note: Threading lock for serializing append operations.

symbols.name: _NON_BODY_FIELDS
symbols.note: Frozenset of position/identity fields excluded from body_sha.

symbols.name: _ALLOWED_TURN_KEYS
symbols.note: Frozenset of accepted top-level turn keys; unknown keys refused loudly.

symbols.name: _ALLOWED_META_KEYS
symbols.note: Frozenset of accepted meta subkeys.

symbols.name: _ALLOWED_PARTICIPANT_KEYS
symbols.note: Frozenset of accepted participant record keys.

symbols.name: _APPEND_CACHE
symbols.note: Dict keyed by resolved store path holding append index, invalidated by file size/mtime.

symbols.name: canonical_body
symbols.note: Returns a new dict containing all record fields except the _NON_BODY_FIELDS set.

symbols.name: canonical_body_json
symbols.note: Returns JSON serialization of canonical_body with sort_keys, compact separators, ensure_ascii.

symbols.name: _body_sha
symbols.note: Returns hex SHA256 of canonical_body_json encoded UTF-8.

symbols.name: _entry_sha
symbols.note: Returns hex SHA256 of prev-or-empty + NUL + body_sha + NUL + ts.

symbols.name: _now_iso
symbols.note: Returns current UTC time as ISO format string.

symbols.name: actor_id
symbols.note: Returns f'council.{vendor}.{model}'.

symbols.name: evidence_ref
symbols.note: Returns dict with path (backslashes converted to forward slashes) and sha256 of the provided bytes.

symbols.name: council_store_path
symbols.note: Validates council_id then returns Path(base_dir or DEFAULT_COUNCIL_DIR) / f'{council_id}.jsonl'.

symbols.name: anchor_path
symbols.note: Returns the store path with '.anchor.json' appended to the file name.

symbols.name: _check_council_id
symbols.note: Raises ValueError if council_id is not a string matching _COUNCIL_ID_RE.

symbols.name: _resolve_store
symbols.note: Resolves the store path and raises ValueError if it resolves under _FORBIDDEN_STORE_DIR.

symbols.name: _scan_paths
symbols.note: Scans each path individually through secret_floor_rule(path, ''), returning first hit.

symbols.name: _scan_texts
symbols.note: Scans each non-empty text individually through secret_floor_rule('', text), returning first hit.

symbols.name: _meta_strings
symbols.note: Returns sorted list of string values from meta dict, skipping empty strings.

symbols.name: _scan_turn
symbols.note: Function body starts at end of chunk; not fully visible.

claims.text: An APPEND-ONLY, HASH-CHAINED JSONL file per council at runs/council/<council_id>.jsonl.
claims.why: The file format and append-only behavior are not implemented in this chunk; only paths and hashing helpers appear.

claims.text: Fail-loud, human-diffable, tamper-evident: every line carries the SHA of the line before it, so a flipped byte or a deleted INTERIOR line breaks the chain and verify_chain NAMES the offending 1-indexed line.
claims.why: verify_chain is in the names-defined-elsewhere list but not present in this chunk; the chaining logic (_entry_sha) is here, but the verification loop is not.

claims.text: TAIL truncation (any prefix of a valid chain is itself a valid chain) is caught only against the head/count ANCHOR persisted beside the transcript and re-checked on every verify.
claims.why: anchor_path exists here, but the actual anchor read/write and verify logic are in functions not present in this chunk.

claims.text: It deliberately REIMPLEMENTS memstore.py's two-SHA discipline instead of importing it, and it must never write to the memory ledger.
claims.why: The chunk defines _body_sha/_entry_sha locally and _resolve_store refuses paths under _FORBIDDEN_STORE_DIR (lines 170-177).

claims.text: Reason, in one line: memstore.fold_state promotes an entry to primary after three independent confirmations, and four models discussing a patch generate confident prose about the codebase -- three agreeing turns would be three confirmations. A mechanism that promotes model opinion to certified memory and then recalls it as fact is the fabrication failure this project treats as the worst one.
claims.why: The claim about memstore.fold_state's promotion logic references another module not supplied; this chunk only shows the refusal mechanism.

claims.text: COUNCIL RECORDS ARE NEVER AN INPUT TO MEMORY RECALL. Any store path under <repo>/memory/ is refused loudly by _resolve_store.
claims.why: _resolve_store raises ValueError when the resolved path is under _FORBIDDEN_STORE_DIR (lines 170-177).

claims.text: body_sha -- sha256 over json.dumps(canonical_body, sort_keys=True, separators=(",",":"), ensure_ascii=True) where canonical_body is the record MINUS the four position/identity fields ts, prev, entry_sha, id (and body_sha itself).
claims.where: module docstring, WHAT IS IN A HASH
claims.why: canonical_body_json uses exactly those arguments (lines 98-100) and _NON_BODY_FIELDS includes ts, prev, entry_sha, id, body_sha (line 63).

claims.text: entry_sha -- sha256(prev + "\0" + body_sha + "\0" + ts), the chain link. Genesis prev is None and folds in as "" (unambiguous: a real prev is always a 64-hex digest).
claims.where: module docstring, WHAT IS IN A HASH
claims.why: _entry_sha builds payload as (prev or "") + "\0" + body_sha + "\0" + ts (lines 104-105). The 64-hex claim about real prev is supported by _SHA256_RE but not enforced here.

claims.text: Unlike memstore, a turn's id is entry_sha[:16], not body_sha[:16], and there is NO dedupe.
claims.where: module docstring, WHAT IS IN A HASH
claims.why: The id assignment and dedupe logic are not in this chunk; only the hashing functions are present.

claims.text: A council transcript is a log of EVENTS: two participants may legitimately emit byte-identical bodies, and deduping the second away would erase a voice from the record.
claims.where: module docstring, WHAT IS IN A HASH
claims.why: The append logic that would implement or avoid dedupe is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Dispatch may be concurrent; CHAINING MUST NOT BE. append_round takes a whole round's turns in ANY completion order, sorts them by the vendor-namespaced actor id, assigns seq at chain time, and stamps ONE chain timestamp for the round.
claims.why: append_round is not present in this chunk; only _WRITE_LOCK and _entry_sha are here.

claims.text: The same fixture responses delivered in reversed completion order therefore produce a byte-identical chain head, so an offline verifier proves "this is the council that happened", not merely "nobody edited this file".
claims.why: Depends on append_round's sorting and timestamp logic, not visible here.

claims.text: Real per-turn wall-clock lives in meta.latency_ms / meta.started_ts, which are body content, not chain position.
claims.why: _ALLOWED_META_KEYS includes latency_ms and started_ts (lines 77-78), and meta is not in _NON_BODY_FIELDS, so it is part of canonical_body.

claims.text: sensitivity.secret_floor_rule has two independent channels and they are fed SEPARATELY here, because a concatenated scan kills the path tier exactly where diffs add secrets.
claims.why: _scan_paths calls secret_floor_rule(str(p), "") per path (lines 185-187) and _scan_texts calls secret_floor_rule("", str(t)) per text (lines 194-197), keeping the two channels separate.

claims.text: PATH channel: every evidence path, INDIVIDUALLY.
claims.why: _scan_paths iterates over paths and calls secret_floor_rule for each one individually (lines 185-187).

claims.text: CONTENT channel: the turn content, every ref, and every metadata string, each scanned on its own -- never over the assembled turn.
claims.why: The call sites that feed content, refs, and metadata into _scan_texts are in _scan_turn, which is cut off at the end of this chunk.

claims.text: This runs on OUTBOUND turns and, critically, on INBOUND vendor responses BEFORE they are chained.
claims.why: The inbound/outbound call sites are in append logic not present in this chunk.

claims.text: A hit REFUSES the turn -- no redact-and-send, no redact-and-store.
claims.why: The refusal action is in _scan_turn or append logic not fully visible here.

claims.text: In its place a status="refused" receipt is chained naming ONLY the rule label (a fixed string, never matched text), so the record still shows WHO was refused and in which round.
claims.why: Receipt construction is in append logic not present in this chunk.

claims.text: The receipt is re-scanned before it is written; if the identity fields themselves carry the secret the receipt degrades to an anonymous one rather than smuggling the credential onto the very path meant to be safe.
claims.why: Receipt re-scanning and degradation logic is not in this chunk.

claims.text: ONE CARVE-OUT, DELIBERATE: withheld (paths an egress lane declined to send) is scanned with the CONTENT channel only, never the path channel.
claims.why: The handling of withheld is in _scan_turn or append logic not present in this chunk.

claims.text: EVERY REQUESTED PARTICIPANT PRODUCES EXACTLY ONE CHAINED TURN PER ROUND -- content, refused, unavailable with a machine reason, or budget_exhausted.
claims.why: The per-participant turn generation is in append logic not present in this chunk.

claims.text: A turn is one of these and nothing else. There is deliberately no "ok" here: a status value that reads as a verdict is one grep away from becoming one.
claims.why: TURN_STATUS tuple contains exactly spoke, refused, unavailable, budget_exhausted, anomaly; no 'ok'.

claims.text: Fail-closed ceiling on a single turn. Transcript tokens grow as O(V^2 R^2), not O(V R); the per-council budget lives in session.py, but no single turn may blow the file up on its own.
claims.why: MAX_CONTENT_CHARS is set to 200_000, a finite ceiling; the growth-rate claim references session.py which is not in this chunk but the constant itself is present.

claims.text: ADR-010 actor-namespace rule, pinned to the MODEL and not just the vendor: "claude said X" is not reproducible six months out, because the model behind a stable command name changes underneath it.
claims.why: _ACTOR_RE pattern requires council.<vendor>.<model> with both vendor and model components; the comment describes the intent and the regex enforces the namespace.

claims.text: Position/identity fields, excluded from body_sha (see module docstring).
claims.why: _NON_BODY_FIELDS contains ts, prev, entry_sha, id, body_sha, exactly matching the docstring's list.

claims.text: Accepted caller keys. A key outside this set is REFUSED loudly, never dropped: a silently dropped field lets two semantically distinct turns canonicalise to the same body and hands the caller a success id for a turn never recorded.
claims.why: The refusal logic that checks keys against _ALLOWED_TURN_KEYS is not in this chunk; only the set definition is present.

claims.text: Per-store append index: tail entry_sha + record/turn counts, keyed by resolved path and invalidated by the file's (size, mtime_ns).
claims.why: _APPEND_CACHE is defined as an empty dict, but the invalidation and usage logic are in append functions not present in this chunk.

claims.text: The content projection body_sha is taken over: everything EXCEPT the position/identity fields. Uniform across turn and roster records so the chain walk needs no per-record-type branch.
claims.why: canonical_body filters out _NON_BODY_FIELDS regardless of record type (lines 96-97).

claims.text: The exact bytes hashed. Exposed so a test can assert determinism against the canonical form rather than against a digest it cannot inspect.
claims.why: canonical_body_json returns the JSON string with deterministic sort_keys and separators (lines 100-102).

claims.text: council.<vendor>.<model> per ADR-010. An unknown model id is recorded as the literal unknown by the CALLER -- never omitted, never inferred.
claims.why: actor_id returns the formatted string (line 113), but the caller's handling of unknown model ids is outside this chunk.

claims.text: One evidence citation: the path as given plus the sha256 of the exact bytes shown to the model. Two participants citing "the file" may have been shown different bytes; without this the transcript records a citation that cannot be reproduced.
claims.why: evidence_ref returns {'path': path with backslashes replaced, 'sha256': sha256 of the provided bytes} (lines 120-121).

claims.text: <base_dir>/<council_id>.jsonl. council_id is filename-safe by validation, not by sanitising: a silently rewritten id would point two councils at one transcript.
claims.why: council_store_path calls _check_council_id which raises on invalid ids (lines 125-126, 142-145), and constructs the path without sanitizing.

claims.text: The head/count anchor beside the transcript. Separate file on purpose: the chain walk cannot detect tail truncation from a truncated file alone.
claims.why: anchor_path returns store_path.with_name(store_path.name + '.anchor.json') (lines 131-133), a separate file.

claims.text: Resolve and REFUSE any path under <repo>/memory/. Council turns must never reach the memory ledger (see module docstring).
claims.why: _resolve_store resolves the path and raises ValueError if it is under _FORBIDDEN_STORE_DIR (lines 163-168).

claims.text: PATH channel, one path at a time -- so a hit is attributable to one path and a diff that ADDS .env cannot hide inside a blob.
claims.why: _scan_paths iterates over each path and calls secret_floor_rule(str(p), "") individually (lines 185-187).

claims.text: CONTENT channel, one string at a time. path="" here is correct and is NOT the forbidden whole-prompt call: the path tier is run separately over every evidence path above, so it is never skipped.
claims.why: _scan_texts calls secret_floor_rule("", str(t)) per text (lines 194-197), and _scan_paths exists separately to run the path tier.

observations.what: _resolve_store returns the unresolved original path p after validation, not the resolved path; callers may then use p which could be relative or contain symlinks, potentially bypassing the memory refusal if the file is accessed via a different path.
_scan_texts skips empty strings with 'continue', so an empty string cannot be flagged; if an empty string were the only carrier of a secret (unlikely), it would pass silently.
_meta_strings only includes string values; non-string metadata values are silently omitted from the scan, potentially letting a secret hide in a non-string field.
The chunk ends mid-function in _scan_turn; the rest of the secret floor logic and all append/verify functions are not visible here.

risks: _resolve_store | medium | Returns original path after validating resolved path; symlink or relative path usage elsewhere could bypass memory refusal | Confirm all callers use the returned path and that file operations resolve it identically

_meta_strings | medium | Non-string meta values are excluded from secret scan, potentially allowing secrets in non-string fields | Check whether meta values are always strings in practice; if not, convert all values before scanning
_scan_texts | low | Empty strings are skipped; if a secret could be an empty string (unlikely), it would pass | Verify secret_floor_rule cannot return a hit for an empty string
chunk cut | low | _scan_turn and append/verify logic not visible; claims about those behaviors are uncheckable | Review remaining chunks
